newsitem.title: CHINA: Production of Deng TV series to be speeded up.
newsitem.headline: Production of Deng TV series to be speeded up.

text.p: Production of a television drama series based on the life of late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, financed by a private company, will be speeded up and released for broadcast in May, company officials said on Sunday.
The six-part series, filmed by the A-Xing Advertising Company in the city of Wenzhou south of Shanghai, is the first private film project on Deng's life made in China, A-Xing's manager Wu Hao said.
He said final permission for the series, originally due for completion in July, had not yet been received from the Ministry of Radio, Film and Television, but added:
"I do not think there will be any problem in getting permission because our script has been read and approved by the authorities already."
The series, named "Stories of Deng Xiaoping", covers Deng's life between 1932 and 1952 and involves investment of about three million yuan ($360,000), he said.
"I cannot be sure if the series will be profitable, that is up to the market to decide, but I don't really care," Wu said.
"The most important thing is that the series can express our respect and thanks for Deng Xiaoping. Without Deng, there would be no today's China and, especially, no today's Wenzhou," he said.

A backward city before 1979, Wenzhou, 350 km (220 miles) south of Shanghai, has boomed since Deng's reforms were launched in the 1980s, and is now considered one of the most capitalist places in China.
